title: Doge and Senate (subscribed Marco Ottobon) to Giovanni Mocenigo, 27 April 1589, BNE Mss/994 ff. 34-38

steps.what: BNE and DECODE image routes tried by script; Cloudflare Turnstile and DECODE login block them.
Catalogue, people, Venetian zifra granda syllabary (Bonavoglia) recorded as a candidate key.
Daniel downloaded the viewer images.
All seven cipher pages transcribed at first pass, 1,528 tokens; clear passages read.
Figure distribution rules out N.11 and matches the 1577-78 Zifra Prima type.
Letter and letter-plus-wildcard annealers on matched synthetic nomenclators recover 0-9 % of letters.
Same annealers on the target give vowel or syllable soup, no separation from shuffles.
DECODE cookie: full-size R2252 images (same BNE scans, ~1.4x the viewer pixels) and keys R1788/R1789/R1790 plus siblings R1843/R1870 fetched; no DOC transcriptions on any.

Zifra Prima per trazer (R1789) transcribed (527 codes) and applied: 94.8% of tokens are defined codes but the decode is not Italian; d83 (commonest token) undefined. Sibling key with same code space, different allocation.
R1790 (c/f/m/r bases, Golfo/Zara cipher), R1870 (Duodo 1595, zifra-granda family) and R1843 (Lippomano 1590) checked: different base sets, not this key.
Zifra Prima with base letters permuted and per-base offsets (coordinate ascent, it-cinquecento LM): only nomenclator-word strings, no text.
CSP Venice viii April 1589 (BHO) checked for a calendar of the 27 April Senate letter: none.

First-pass digit statistics show systematic misreading (7 read as 2, 8 as 0, 3/5/8 confused); with those re-readings the Zifra Prima decodes frequent tokens to the commonest units and passages read as Italian; syllable-usage correlation p=0.0008 vs structured null.
Zifra Prima (R1789) confirmed as this letter's key, unchanged so far: e.g. f.35r ll.16-17 'alcun soccorso per proveder ... al pericolo di quella corona'.

beam.py: per-token Viterbi over digit-confusion variants with the Zifra Prima, it-cinquecento 5-gram with optional word spaces, EM-estimated confusion costs; machine draft Italian in long stretches (draft_beam_v1.txt).
Hand reading begun line by line from candidates + DECODE line crops (rd_f35r.txt; two helper agents on ff.35v-36v and ff.37r-38r); c86 = o and d83 = a found from context (keys/ottobon_overrides.tsv).

Hand reading complete for all 7 pages (rd_*.txt): 721 of 1,566 tokens read as Italian (46%, measure_rd.py); ff.37r-38r 56-72%, f.35r 63%, ff.35v-36v 12-17% (digits unresolvable at the available resolution).
Corpus for the LM: Alberi, Relazioni degli ambasciatori veneti (9 vols, archive.org djvu text) added to the it-cinquecento sources with the shared lang engine (build_venlm.py; 47 M chars).

dec.py: noisy-channel decoder (digit/base confusion model and code prior estimated from the 721 hand-read tokens, Venetian 5-gram LM, vectorised Viterbi beam over whole pieces, skip option, per-token margins). Leave-one-page-out calibration against the hand reading: 644/721 = 89.3% agreement by value vs 65.9% identity baseline and 73.8% at beam.py's weights.

Synthetic test (dec.py sim: hand-read runs re-corrupted by sampling the channel, 627 tokens): 82.6% recovered at 55% identity, 61% at 40%; word-lexicon bonus and self-training EM gave no gain; margin calibration: margin >= 2 agrees 97-100% with the hand reading.
Free decoding of ff.35v-36v gives Italian fragments but no continuous sense (dec_out/, view.py); the decoder alone does not read those pages.

Print search (CSP Venice viii, Hubner Sixte-Quint ii-iii, Desjardins v, Morosini Historia Veneta, De Thou): no verbatim text of the letter or of the Senate's answer; Hubner iii no. 36 (Doge to Badoer 13 May 1589) and ii p. 236 (29 April) give parallel wording only. De Maisse's letter-book with the answers is BL Add MS 30635-30637 (not digitised).

fit.py/refit.py: crib fit of proposed Italian line texts (hand reading, decoder drafts, context) onto the first-pass tokens; a token is read only outside gaps with channel log-prob >= -5; 74 lines re-read (texts_reread.txt).

fitcontrol.py: each text fitted onto wrong lines (15 shifts): 10% of tokens fit by chance at threshold -5 (22% at -8, 5% at -3) vs 80% on the true lines; 5 lines with weak evidence (true <= control max + 2) demoted to low.

Re-measured (measure_rd.py): 981 of 1,565 tokens read (62.7%), from 721 (46.0%); f.38r 84%, f.37v 79%, f.37r 70%, f.35r 68%, f.35v 48%, f.36r 35%, f.36v 29%. New: f.35v ll.7-9 'collegarsi et stringersi maggiormente in qualche unione di lega'; f.37r ll.15-17 'quanto alle richieste fateci da Vostra [...] in nome di quel Serenissimo Re' (second piece = the answer to the French ambassador).
Siblings checked on DECODE (R2248-R2262, Mss/994 items 1-15): no other Venetian cipher and no decipherment; ff.38v-63v in R2252 are address and blank leaves.

Venetian LM registered in lang/ as it-venezia (source it-relazioni, double weight); dec.py now loads it. Leave-one-page-out calibration against the 981 re-read tokens (ALPHA 0.4, BETA 0.4, CLEN 0.3): 870/981 = 88.7% with the registered model and with the old local table alike. Note: these reference tokens include the crib-fit re-reading, so the figure is not independent of the decoder's channel model; the independent figure is the 89.3% against the 721 hand-read tokens.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): first-pass transcriptions ct_f35r-ct_f38r, page readings rd_f35r-rd_f38r and the joined Italian reading.txt, in two entries for the two pieces; key keys/zifra_prima_R1789.tsv with keys/ottobon_overrides.tsv

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): reading.txt read through: the second piece (ff. 37r-38r) builds Italian sentences with scattered holes (kept read, reviewed B); the first piece (ff. 35r-36v) is mostly [...] and low lines, relabelled decoded, not read. fraction_read 0.627 -> 0.525 (tokens in the piece that reads).

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The Council of Ten's Zifra Prima key sheet (DECODE R1789) fits the letter; the noisy first-pass transcription was re-read against the key by hand and by a calibrated noisy-channel decoder and crib fit (dec.py, fit.py); Italian read in part.
outcome.notes: Key: R1789 plus d83 = a, c86 = o. Content: Senate's reply to a French request for aid to Henry III: intercession with Sixtus V. Valle de la Cerda's contemporary solution is lost.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Reading audit 22 Oct 2026: tokens of the piece that reads as sentences, ff. 37r-38r = 820 of 1,563 (ct_f*.txt word counts: 341 + 363 + 116); the first piece, ff. 35r-36v (743), is decoded, not read. Withdrawn as a reading figure: 0.627 = rd_f35r..rd_f38r.txt via measure_rd.py: tokens in high/medium lines without '?' (981/1,565), after the dec.py/fit.py crib-fit re-reading of 9 Oct 2026.

gaps.item: ff.35v-36v, 316 tokens in lines without anchoring sense
gaps.detail: first-pass digits too corrupt for the decoder or a crib fit; the BNE scan (~130-180 dpi) does not separate 2/7, 3/5/8, 0/8; needs a 400-dpi BNE reproduction or the register copy (ASVe Senato Secreta, Deliberazioni Francia 1589, 27 April)

gaps.item: f.35r, 69 tokens (ll.1-3 and 12, plus gaps in read lines)
gaps.detail: stain at the head of f.35r; no better image than the BNE scan

gaps.item: ff.37r-38r, 199 tokens (f.37r ll.1-2, 7, 10, 22, 24; f.37v ll.1, 3; gaps in read lines)
gaps.detail: unresolved digits and gutter losses; the second piece's text (the Senate's answer to de Maisse) should be in BL Add MS 30635 (de Maisse's letters 'avec les responses', not digitised) and the ASVe register

credits.note: Council of Ten Zifra Prima of 1577-78 (ASVe CX Cifre b. 4 reg. 16 ff. 64-65, DECODE R1789), plus two homophones found here
his description of the Zifra Prima (b. 4 r. 16 f. 64, DECODE R1789) matched the letter's design and led to the key

texts.label: First piece, ff. 35r-36v: the Senate to Mocenigo, 27 April 1589
texts.note: reading.txt ff. 35r-36v: f. 35r builds a few clauses (the French request for help), but ff. 35v-36v are mostly [...] and (low) lines with fragments ("assicurar ... dalli ne ... che ..."); holes in most sentences
texts.summary: The Senate tells its ambassador Giovanni Mocenigo that the French ambassador, setting out the troubles and needs of Henry III, asked Venice to help him (with the Emperor) against the imminent danger to the crown, and sends a copy of its answer. Read only in part: ff. 35v-36v are mostly unread because the digits are unresolved on the available images.

texts.label: Second piece, ff. 37r-38r: copy of the Senate's answer to the French request

reading_review.note: reading.txt ff. 37r-38r: the Senate's answer reads as continuous Italian sentences (the affection the Republic bears the crown of France; it will interpose with the Pope so that His Holiness favours His Most Christian Majesty in quieting the risings of that kingdom) with scattered [...] and line-end gaps; only f. 37r ll. 1-2 and f. 37v ll. 1, 3 are low.

texts.summary: The Senate assures Henry III of the Republic's affection for the French crown and resolves to interpose its intercession with Sixtus V, so that the Pope will favour the King's just cause in quieting the risings in his kingdom and quenching the fire of war, weeks before the monitorium against Henry III of 24 May 1589.

prior.where: Valle de la Cerda read it c. 1589 but the solution is lost
